title: Lauren Templeton VALUEx BRK 2026
description:
Why Fairfax Financial Looks Like Berkshire Circa 1997 The case for Fairfax as today's young Berkshire: $26B equity, $40.8B float, 18.7% book-value CAGR since 1985, and family control.

See the full stream of the event here: https://youtube.com/live/V3V7bqLGP9o
summary: The speaker argues that Fairfax Financial currently exhibits the same structural DNA and growth potential as Berkshire Hathaway did 30 years ago, specifically noting that Fairfax is small enough to move meaningfully while maintaining a decentralized culture with long-tenured management. The presentation claims that Fairfax has already completed its transformation since 2017, evidenced by a compound annual growth rate of 18.6% and a balance sheet with 40.8 billion in float generating over 2.5 billion in annual interest and dividends alone.
